title: No tanto... como: matizar una comparación

sections.content: No tanto X como Y (not so much X as Y) reframes what actually happened, rejecting an expected or simpler explanation in favor of a more precise one -- exactly what a closing synthesis needs when the obvious verdict ("the revolution transformed society") isn't quite accurate. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El legado institucional de esta revolución no fue tanto una transformación completa e inmediata de la sociedad como la creación de un partido político dominante.
items.english: This revolution's institutional legacy was not so much a complete and immediate transformation of society as the creation of a dominant political party.

items.spanish: El resultado no fue tanto una sociedad plenamente igualitaria como una estabilidad política notable.
items.english: The result was not so much a fully egalitarian society as remarkable political stability.

items.spanish: México evitó el ciclo de golpes de Estado y dictaduras militares que sufrieron muchos de sus vecinos.
items.english: Mexico avoided the cycle of coups and military dictatorships that many of its neighbors suffered.

items.spanish: El legado de la Revolución mexicana no fue tanto un final feliz y definitivo como el comienzo de un experimento institucional único.
items.english: The legacy of the Mexican Revolution was not so much a happy, definitive ending as the beginning of a unique institutional experiment.

sections.content: Unlike tanto... como (both... and, section 5 of the previous unit), no tanto... como sets up a contrast, not an equivalence -- it says the second thing is the more accurate description, not that both are equally true.
